land.text: the Urartian lands, whose capital Van the Medes 'took over' in 590 BC (without the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid, Assyrian-held since 743)

successors.note: Urartu page: 'The Medes then took over the Urartian capital of Van in 590 BC, effectively ending the sovereignty of Urartu.' The same page and its infobox also allow an Achaemenid conquest in 547 (Cyrus); Cliopatria keeps Urartu to 551. The dossier follows the 590 sentence.

land.text: the Satrapy of Armenia that 'had replaced' the Kingdom of Van by the late 6th century

successors.note: Second successor named in the infobox ('Median Empire; Achaemenid Empire; Satrapy of Armenia'); it comes after the Median phase and is not part of the 590 hand-over. The Orontid Armenia that followed is traced in kingdom-of-armenia.

capitals.name: Sugunia, then Arzashkun
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Sugunia; Arzashkun; Tushpa (after 832 BC)'. The page does not locate Sugunia or Arzashkun (Shalmaneser III took both); the dot is parked at Tushpa as a stand-in.

capitals.name: Tushpa (Van)
capitals.note: 'Sarduri I ... moved the capital to Tushpa (modern Van, Turkey, on the shore of Lake Van)'. Fortresses at Erebuni (782), Argishtihinili (776), Karmir Blur (Teishebaini) and Ayanis are outposts, not capitals.

correction.text: the Lake Van core of the unified kingdom of Arame (c. 860-843): the page says the kingdom 'was centred around Lake Van' and that Sarduri I made Tushpa, 'on the shore of Lake Van', the capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Urartu shape begins in 800 (53,104 km2) but the page puts the kingdom's establishment at 860 BC (infobox) under Arame. The page gives no extent for the 9th century; Van province plus the lake is the minimal reading of 'centred around Lake Van'. Ispuini's annexation of Musasir (c. 820-800) is not drawn: the page does not locate Musasir (see notes).

53,104 km2 for 800-751, bbox 41.30-46.11 E, 38.29-40.29 N, the Van basin and the Ararat plain. The page says Menua 'enlarged the kingdom greatly' and that Argishti I 'added more territories along the Aras and Lake Sevan' (Erebuni founded 782, Argishtihinili 776); the shape's northern edge, 40.29 N, only reaches the south shore of Lake Sevan, so it is plausible for the early part and understated for 782-751. No area or border is given for these reigns, so the shape stands; the ledger's 782 gain carries the growth.

correction.text: without the west bank of the Euphrates round Kummuh and Melid: the 743 BC battle was fought 'somewhere in Kummuh' and Tiglath-pileser III forced 'the Urartians back across the Euphrates'; Kummuh/Melid is an Urartian vassal tint only for 750-743 and Assyrian-held after

keyframe_review.note: 160,486 km2 for 750-701, bbox west to 37.29 E (beyond the Euphrates), east to 46.14 E (Tabriz and Lake Urmia, which the Urartu page gives as the peak: 'east to present-day Tabriz, Lake Urmia, and beyond'). The Urartu page also says the kingdom covered 'approximately 200,000 square miles (520,000 km2)' with no date and a citation-needed reach 'almost to the shores of the Black Sea'; Cliopatria's 160,486 is a factor 3.2 below that undated figure, so the figure or the shape is wrong. The shape is kept (the figure is uncited and the Black Sea reach is flagged on the page) but trimmed west of the Euphrates, where the Sarduri II page puts the 743 defeat.

correction.text: the 615 shape as the bridge, without the west bank of the Euphrates round Kummuh and Melid that the -750 keyframe removes: no page and no ledger event gives it back to Urartu after 743 (Sarduri II page: Tiglath-pileser III forced 'the Urartians back across the Euphrates'; the page is silent on any later recovery). The Urartu page says Argishti II (714-685) 'restored the kingdom' against the Cimmerians and Rusa II (685-645) presided over 'development and prosperity' but gives no extent for 700-616

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Urartu shape for 700-616 although the page lists kings through these years (Argishti II 714-685, Rusa II 685-645, Rusa III 620-609) and fortresses of Rusa II (Karmir Blur, Ayanis). The 701 and 615 shapes have the same bbox (west edge 37.29/37.28 E) and area (160,486 and 161,552 km2), so the 615 shape is used as the bridge; confidence is low, the page is silent on borders. Repair (review eu-19-a): the first draft used the 615 shape whole, which put the 16,438 km2 round Kummuh and Melid back into Urartu in 700 without an event; the Euphrates strip is now cut out as in the 750 keyframe. Re-read 2026-10-31: the Sarduri II page says the 743 battle forced 'the Urartians back across the Euphrates' and does not say that the land was regained; the Urartu page does not mention Kummuh at all.

161,552 km2 for 615-601 as drawn by Cliopatria: Rusa III (620-609) and Rusa IV (609-590) on the page; the page gives no border. Adjusted (review eu-19-a): the Cliopatria shape still contains the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid (65 cells, about 16,438 km2), which the 750 keyframe removes after the 743 defeat; with no event that regains it, the strip stays out. Rest of the shape stands.

correction.text: the 615 shape without the west bank of the Euphrates round Kummuh and Melid (Assyrian-held from 743; no page returns it to Urartu)

shape unchanged for 600-590 apart from the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid (Assyrian-held from 743, as in the 750 and 615 keyframes): valid to 590, the year the Medes 'took over the Urartian capital of Van'; after 590 the land is Median (Cliopatria keeps the Urartu name to 551)

keyframe_review.note: 154,709 km2 for 600-551. The page: 'The Medes then took over the Urartian capital of Van in 590 BC, effectively ending the sovereignty of Urartu'; the Median Empire page agrees that 'before 590 BCE, the Medes had already subjugated Mannea and Urartu', while the Urartu infobox also allows Achaemenid conquest in 547. The years 589-551 of this shape are therefore Median (median-kingdom) land, not Urartian; the colour should end in 590. Repair (review eu-19-a): the same Euphrates strip (about 16,438 km2) is cut out of the 600 shape so that the 750, 700, 615 and 600 keyframes agree.

region.text: the Nairi states and tribes, unified around Lake Van

ledger.note: c. 860: the Nairi tribes are unified as the kingdom of Urartu under King Arame. 'The Nairi states and tribes became unified kingdom under King Arame of Urartu (c. 860–843 BC)'; infobox 'Established: 860 BC'. The page gives no extent; the region is the Van basin.
c. 832: Sarduri I founds a new dynasty. 'Sarduri I (c. 832–820 BC), the son of Lutipri, established a new dynasty' (the state, its colour and its dossier continue).
c. 832: the capital moves to Tushpa (Van). 'moved the capital to Tushpa (modern Van, Turkey, on the shore of Lake Van)'; infobox 'Tushpa (after 832 BC)'.

region.text: north to Lake Sevan, much of Diauehi and the Ararat Valley

ledger.note: 782: Argishti I takes the Ararat plain and the Sevan side. 'He expanded his kingdom north to Lake Sevan, conquering much of Diauehi and the Ararat Valley'; 'He founded the citadel of Erebuni in 782 BC' (Armavir's Argishtihinili followed in 776). The page dates the founding, not the conquest, so 782 is the year of the first fortress on the new land. Menua's earlier victory over Diauehi's King Utuburshini, who 'became a vassal paying tribute', is on the Menua page, undated.

region.text: Kummuh and Melid in the Euphrates valley, gained by Sarduri II

ledger.note: c. 750: Sarduri II's Euphrates gains, Melid and Kummuh, are tribute-paying land. The Sarduri II page (reign 764-735) gives no year for the gain, only the 743 defeat; 750 is the year of the Cliopatria jump from 53,104 to 160,486 km2 and agrees with the Kummuh dossier's 'around 750'.

region.text: the peak extent 'east to present-day Tabriz, Lake Urmia, and beyond'

ledger.note: c. 750: the peak. The Urartu page names no conquered state for the east; the Sarduri II page has a campaign against Mannai 'whose population was exiled to Biaina'. The Menua, Argishti I and Sarduri II reigns (c. 810-735) together built the 160,486 km2 Cliopatria shape; the page gives no year for the Lake Urmia side, so the jump is dated to the Cliopatria shape change.

region.text: Kummuh, where the battle was fought

ledger.note: 743: Assyria strikes at Urartu's Euphrates bridgehead. 'In 743 BC, at a battle located somewhere in Kummuh, the Assyrians, under Tiglath-pileser III, defeated Sarduri and his anti-Assyrian coalition'. The Urartu page puts the defeat in 745, 'the first year' of Tiglath-Pileser III.

region.text: Kummuh and Melid, 'forcing the Urartians back across the Euphrates'

ledger.note: 743: Urartu is pushed back across the Euphrates and loses Kummuh. The page gives the battle, not the end of tribute; the year is the battle's.
743: a single battle decides it; the page records no further fighting for the zone.

region.text: Lake Urmia, where Rusa I was defeated, and Musasir, whose temple was sacked

ledger.note: 714: Sargon II's campaign. 'In 714 BC, the Urartian kingdom suffered heavily from Cimmerian raids and the campaigns of Sargon II'; 'the Urartian king Rusa I was crushingly defeated by Sargon II at Lake Urmia' and the Musasir temple was sacked.
714: the campaign ends the same year; the page records no Assyrian annexation, and Cliopatria draws no change in the Urartu shape.

region.text: the Urartian kingdom as it stood when Van fell, without the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid

ledger.note: 590: Van falls and Urartu ends. 'The Medes then took over the Urartian capital of Van in 590 BC, effectively ending the sovereignty of Urartu.' Infobox: 'Median conquest (or Achaemenid conquest in 547): 590 BC/547 BC'; Median Empire page: 'the general consensus is that Urartu was destroyed by the Medes in the late 7th century BCE'.

wars.name: Battle of Kummuh (Tiglath-Pileser III against Sarduri II's coalition)

zones.text: Kummuh and Melid on the Euphrates

wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Sarduri II and his anti-Assyrian coalition were beaten 'somewhere in Kummuh' and Urartu was forced back across the Euphrates.
wars.note: The Urartu page dates Tiglath-Pileser III's victory to 745, 'the first year of his reign'; the Sarduri II page, followed here, to 743.

wars.name: Sargon II's campaign against Urartu

zones.text: Lake Urmia and the temple city of Musasir

wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Rusa I 'crushingly defeated' at Lake Urmia and the Musasir temple sacked; no annexation is stated, and Urartu recovered under Argishti II (714-685).
wars.note: The same page puts Cimmerian raids in 714; the Cimmerian and later Scythian attacks (undated, 'constant attacks' after Rusa II) are the background to the decline.

wars.name: Median conquest of Urartu
wars.outcome: The Medes, with the Scythians, overran Urartu and took its capital Van in 590 BC, ending its sovereignty.
wars.note: The pages date only the two ends: 612 (Cyaxares, Nabopolassar and the Scythians 'conquered Assyria', immediately before the invasion sentence) and 590 (Van). The Median Empire page says the date of the conquest is not recorded ('written sources end after 640 BCE') and that Cyrus' later campaign against Urartu is a minority view. Re-read 2026-10-31: the Urartu page has the invasion without a year: 'Late during the 7th century BC (during or after Sarduri III's reign), Urartu was invaded by Scythians and their allies—the Medes.' Before it, 'it became dependent on Assyria, as evidenced by Rusa II's son Sarduri III (645–635 BC) referring to the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal as his "father"'. The war is kept as this one entry rather than a ledger contest (confidence 1: the invasion has no year and no zone beyond 'Urartu', and the 612 and 590 ends are the pages' own); sibling scythia /ledger/5 gains all Urartu in 635 and the Urartu page does not support that year or a conquest by the Scythians alone.

certainty.note: Urartian borders are known from royal inscriptions and fortresses, not from lines; the page gives no treaty or survey frontier, so every edge stays soft.

sources.title: Urartu
sources.note: Identity, capitals, dates (860, 832, 782, 745, 714, 590), succession; the 520,000 km2 body figure is undated.

sources.title: Menua
sources.note: Reign (c. 810-786, death 780 in one sentence), the Diauehi victory; no campaign years.

sources.title: Argishti I
sources.note: Reign 786-764, Erebuni 782, Argishtihinili 776, the conquest of Diauehi, Sevan and the Ararat Valley.

sources.title: Sarduri II
sources.note: Reign 764-735, peak, Melid and Kummuh, the 743 battle 'in Kummuh'.

sources.title: Median Empire
sources.note: Urartu's end by the Medes, 612, 590 and 585 context.

notes: Cliopatria row Kingdom of Urartu, 4 shapes (800-751, 750-701, 615-601, 600-551): the row lacks 860-801 (new keyframe) and 700-616 (new keyframe, bridged at low confidence) and runs to 551 although the page ends Urartian sovereignty in 590 (verdict adjust). Page budget (5): Urartu, Menua, Argishti I, Sarduri II, Median Empire. NOT MAPPED because the pages do not locate the places: Ispuini's annexation of Musasir (c. 820-800), Menua's victory over Diauehi's King Utuburshini, and Sarduri II's conquest of 'the northern region of' Colchis (the Colchis page says Qulha's location is disputed, west Georgia or near Göle). Gazetteer names needed: Musasir (place), Diauehi (region). Disagreements: reign dates differ between infobox and body (Arame 858-844/860-843, Sarduri I 834-828/832-820, Menua 810-785/800-785, Rusa III 629-590/620-609); Sarduri II's defeat 743 (Sarduri II page) or 745 (Urartu page); end 590 or 547. Sibling dossiers record an Assyrian suzerainty over Urartu 645-635 (neo-assyrian-empire /ledger/48-49) and a Scythian gain of Urartu in 635 (scythia /ledger/5). The Urartu page has both in outline and they are not in this ledger on purpose: 'As a result, it became dependent on Assyria, as evidenced by Rusa II's son Sarduri III (645–635 BC) referring to the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal as his "father"' (the suzerain holds the vassal tint under the schema, so Urartu needs no vassal event), and 'Late during the 7th century BC (during or after Sarduri III's reign), Urartu was invaded by Scythians and their allies—the Medes.' (no year; kept as the war 'Median conquest of Urartu', not as a contest event). The median-kingdom dossier has no Urartu event: the 590 hand-over is recorded here only. The infobox area is absent; the body figure (520,000 km2) is undated and a factor 3.2 above Cliopatria's maximum. Repair 2026-10-31 (review eu-19-a): the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid (Commagene plus Malatya 100 km, 65 cells, about 16,438 km2) is cut out of the 700, 615 and 600 keyframes as it already was from 750, because the Sarduri II page has Urartu pushed 'back across the Euphrates' in 743 and no page or event gives the land back.
